You’ve got a final round with Lincoln International for an analyst role. Here’s a focused plan, likely question types, and concise practice prompts so you can rehearse answers now.

One next step: tell me how long the interview is and who you’ll meet (titles) if you know it — otherwise I’ll assume a 45–60 minute interview with a senior associate and a VP covering technical case, fit and market knowledge.
What they’ll want (short)
- Technical competence: accounting, valuation (DCF, comps), LBO basics, modeling logic and math under pressure.
- Transaction judgment: deal process, client interaction, commercial sense.
- Fit and behavior: teamwork, long hours, learning quickly, attention to detail.
- Market awareness: why Lincoln, recent deals, sector interest.
10-point prep plan (do these in order)
1. Re-read the job posting or any interviewer notes you have. (If you want I can fetch the posting — paste it or tell me where.)
2. Brush accounting fundamentals: walk through a simple three-statement link (how NI flows to cash; working capital items).
3. DCF quick checklist: drivers (revenue growth, margins), WACC basics, terminal value methods and sensitivity table.
4. Comps and precedent logic: how to pick comps, adjust for size and growth, apply multiples.
5. LBO basics: sources & uses, IRR drivers, debt paydown, covenant risk.
6. Case practice: time yourself on a 20–30 minute short case (5–7 slides) — structure, key assumptions, conclusion.
7. Fit stories: prepare 5 STAR stories (team conflict, leadership, error you caught, tight deadline, why M&A).
8. Market read: prepare 2-3 recent Lincoln deals or industry-relevant transactions and one insight on what mattered (price drivers, buyer type).
9. Questions to ask: deal process at Lincoln, training/exit paths, recent sector strategy — 3-5 crisp questions.
10. Logistics: set your camera, test audio, have a one-page cheat sheet (not shown) with formulas and deal facts.
Top technical refresh (short answers to know)
- Walk me through a three-statement model: (one-paragraph walkthrough: revenue → EBIT → tax → NI → addbacks → CFO → CFI/CFI link → ending cash; working capital changes affect CFO).
- DCF vs comps: DCF gives intrinsic value from cash flows; comps give market benchmark; use both and reconcile differences.
- How to pick comps: same industry, similar size/growth/margins, same geography and buyer set; adjust for non-recurring items.
- What moves IRR in an LBO: purchase price, exit multiple, leverage amount, margin improvement, holding period.
- What is WACC: weighted average of cost of equity and after-tax cost of debt; sensitive to capital structure and beta.

Behavioral answers — structure to use
- One-sentence context, your role and actions (concrete specifics), one measurable result or learning.
Example prompts to practice now (answer as you would in the room; I’ll score and rewrite)
1) Tell me about a time you found an error in a model under time pressure.
2) Describe a deal you worked on and the part you owned.
3) Why Lincoln International? Why this sector/coverage group?
4) Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate and what you did.
5) Walk me through a valuation you completed and one assumption you would defend.
Case format likely in final round
- Short written case or modeling test (45–90 minutes) OR oral case with deck and Q&A.
- Typical ask: value a company, recommend buyer/exit strategy, identify 3 key value-creation levers.
- Structure: 1) clarify objective and time, 2) list information you need and assumptions, 3) build a quick story (3-4 slides: summary, key assumptions, valuation range, recommendation + risks).
Quick checklist for the day
- One-page outline of your 3 best fit stories.
- 2-3 recent Lincoln deals or public M&A deals in target sector.
- Calculator open, Excel template for quick DCF or LBO (simple drivers).
- Water, charged laptop, quiet place, backup internet.
- 1-sentence closing: “I’m excited by Lincoln because X, and I can add value by Y.”

Practice offer
Start with this: pick one of the practice prompts above and answer it now in one to three minutes. I’ll score it on structure, evidence and specificity and give one concrete improvement, then prompt the next question. Which prompt do you want to practice first?

replies:
You don't have any applications or an apply-queue on file yet. The one step that starts this is: tell me which job (paste the job link or the posting ID from a posting I found), or let me search for jobs for the role and city you want.
When you pick the first posting, I will read that posting and then prepare an application card for your approval. Here's exactly what I'll include on that prepared card — field by field — and what I will put in each field by default or where I'll ask you to supply text. I assumed a standard employer careers form and an application card; if the posting asks for additional items (portfolio link, GitHub, references, visa status, pay expectations, work authorization documents), I will add those fields too when I read the posting.

Fields I will prepare on the application card and what goes in each:
1) Employer / Job title
- What I fill: the posting's exact company name and title as shown on the posting.
- You don't edit this on the card; it's pulled from the posting.

2) Location / Remote
- What I fill: the posting's place or "remote" as listed.
- If the posting lists multiple locations I show them exactly.

3) Posting link / posting reference
- What I fill: the posting's link and the posting's reference I retrieved from the job board.
4) Resume (PDF) to attach
- What I fill: I will attach a tailored PDF resume using only your confirmed facts for that specific posting. If you have no confirmed facts or no saved resume contact, I'll attach nothing and prompt you to paste or confirm your resume/contact. I will not invent or add draft facts to the resume until you confirm them.
- Where you'll act: if no tailored resume can be produced, you must paste your resume or confirm facts first.
5) Cover letter / message (if the application has a free-text "cover note" or an email)
- What I prepare: a concise cover note (≤120 words) tailored to the posting using your confirmed facts and the posting's top skill words. Any [brackets] mark missing specifics I couldn't confirm (e.g., [manager name], [start date], [specific metric]).
- You can edit it in the card before approval.
6) Answers to screening questions (yes/no or short text)
- What I fill: I pre-fill truthful answers from your confirmed facts (e.g., work authorization, willingness to relocate, salary expectations) when those facts exist on file. If a screening question relates to something not on file, I leave it blank with a suggested default and show it for your approval.
- I will never guess answers you haven't confirmed.

7) Work authorization / visa status
- What I fill: if you have a confirmed fact about authorization, it goes here. If none on file, I leave it blank and prompt you to supply it.
8) Earliest start date / notice period
- What I fill: blank unless you have supplied a confirmed fact; I will propose a sensible default (e.g., "2 weeks" or "30 days") and mark it as editable.

9) Salary / compensation expectations (if asked)
- What I fill: blank unless you give a number now. I can also fill "not listed" if the posting has pay not shown, or the posting's listed pay if present. I will not invent your desired salary.

10) Portfolio / GitHub / work samples (links)
- What I fill: links you confirmed on file. If none, I leave the field blank and propose you add any public links.
11) Attachments (transcript, certifications, writing sample)
- What I fill: only files you have confirmed are on file. I will note required attachments from the posting and leave them unfilled until you supply them.

12) References
- What I fill: nothing unless you supply reference names and emails now; I will list the posting's request for references as a reminder.

13) Diversity / voluntary demographic fields
- What I fill: I leave these blank; you fill them when you approve the card if you wish.
14) Resume header contact (name, email, phone)
- What I fill: only if you used the resume-contact step before. Otherwise blank; I will ask "What name and email should go at the top of your resume?" before finalizing the attached resume.

15) Short answers to open prompts (e.g., "Why do you want to join?")
- What I prepare: a 2–3 sentence tailored answer using confirmed facts and posting signals, with [brackets] for any missing specifics that I didn't have.
16) External application steps note
- What I include: if the posting requires application on an external site (Greenhouse, Lever, company portal), I include the exact next step and note any one-time codes or captchas they will have to complete themselves.

17) Final verification checklist and notes to you
- What I include: a checklist of things you must confirm before I queue the application: resume contact, work authorization answer, start date, salary answer (if required), and any required attachments.
What I will not do
- I will not submit the application. I will only prepare the card with every field populated from the posting and your confirmed facts or left blank with a clear prompt.
- I will not invent any facts (experience, dates, salary, authorization) you haven't given and confirmed.
- I will not attach or change files on your account without your approval in the extension.

Next step: paste the job link or the posting reference for the posting you mean, or say "search for [role] in [city]" and I'll find the first posting and prepare the card. One question: do you want me to include a short cover note (≤120 words) on the card by default?
